title: Activation View hidden-coordinate symmetry audit
hypothesis: For a two-layer residual linear block f(x)=x+W2 W1 x, an invertible hidden coordinate G preserves the exact input-output function if W1 becomes G W1 and W2 becomes W2 G^-1. Such a reparameterization is a gauge orbit, not an additional logical function. Changing only W1 should change outputs.
physical_object: One deterministic two-layer residual linear block with input/output width 32 and hidden width 64 in FP32.
mirror_coordinate: Invertible hidden-coordinate transform G, tested as permutation/sign, positive diagonal scale, and dense orthogonal QR transform.
logical_multiplicity: Count only output-distinct functions; invariance is zero new functions.
controls: paired native reparameterization G W1 and W2 G^-1
unpaired transform G W1 with W2 fixed

metrics: relative RMS and max absolute output difference
actual serialized bytes with G and inverse

fresh.opening_rule: Open if both development seeds show paired relative RMS <=1e-5, unpaired functional change >1e-5, and condition number >=0.25.

compute.report: matrix MAC count and per-artifact serialization time; no training

gates.NOT_ESTABLISHED: The exact gauge mechanism can be demonstrated, but no useful Mirror application or capacity/compression claim is supported by this fixed linear screen.

boundaries: Synthetic linear mechanism only; no trained Transformer or semantic task.
A function-preserving symmetry is not additional functional capacity.
Transformed maps are fully serialized; no free reconstruction state.
